content.text:
This Outlook Scheduling Assistant screenshot shows the free/busy times of six attendees and the room NYC-14 Liberty (10) on Monday and Tuesday (all times New York time). I need to book a 60-minute meeting. Rules: Priya Shah and Marcus Lee are required; at least 2 of the other four (Nate Russo, Elena Ruiz, Rachel Cohen and Kenji Watanabe) must also be able to attend; tentative (hatched) blocks count as free, while busy and out-of-office blocks count as busy; the meeting must not overlap the 12:00-13:00 lunch hour; the room row must be free for the whole meeting; the meeting must lie within 9:00-17:00 and start on a quarter hour. What is the earliest start time that satisfies every rule? Answer as the day and the 24-hour start time, in the form `Tue 09:45` (three-letter day, HH:MM with a leading zero).

Think step by step. Then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>

message.content:
- Monday’s room is free at 09:00 and 09:15, but neither full hour has two available optional attendees. Later morning slots are blocked by the room or the lunch-hour rule, and the afternoon has no hour when both required attendees and the room are free.
- On Tuesday, the room is busy until 09:30. The 09:30 and 09:45 starts don’t work: only Rachel is available for the full hour among the four optional attendees.
- At 10:15, Priya and Marcus are free (Marcus’s block is tentative), the room is free through 11:15, and Rachel and Kenji can attend. This is the earliest qualifying slot.

FINAL ANSWER: Tue 10:15
